fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to allow responders to quickly identify the property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entry point with high-visibility posts or reflective delineators so it remains identifiable at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse and exit without backing the full length of the drive.
• Trim dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear travel width for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back overhanging branches above the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for ladder trucks and other tall emergency vehicles.
• Thin dense vegetation bordering the open green space to reduce obstructions that could slow responder movement around the property.
• Mark or label the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency.
• Keep any gate on the perimeter fencing unlocked or equipped with a knox box to allow responders to enter without delay.
• Identify and mark a secondary staging area in the open terrain where additional emergency vehicles can park without blocking the access drive.
• Trim landscaped plantings that obstruct sightlines between the access drive and the main residence entrance.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin trees on all sides of the structure to create open space between the canopy and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing beneath tree canopies near the structure to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the trees.
• Cut and remove grass around the structure, keeping it short and dry grass cleared away from the building.
• Separate clusters of shrubs and trees near the structure by removing individual plants between groupings to break up continuous vegetation.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from within the mixed vegetation areas closest to the structure.
• Thin shrubs along the length of the driveway so vehicles, including emergency trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim tree branches that overhang the driveway to allow full clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, dead grass, and loose debris along its full length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching from the main road.
• Keep a turning area or pull-out available near the structure so emergency vehicles are not trapped on the single access route.
• Remove shrubs and tall grass from the edges of the driveway to reduce the chance of fire crossing onto the road surface.
